chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Aban and others, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled regarding the son of mula'anah that his mother inherits one-third of him, and the remainder belongs to the Imam, because liability for his offense rests upon the Imam.

key_terms.لِلْإِمَامِ: belonging to the Imam as the remaining share
key_terms.ٱبْنِ ٱلْمُلَاعَنَةِ: the son connected to a case of mutual imprecation (li'an)

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling for the son of li'an in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning the inheritance of the son born in a case of li'an. It states that his mother receives one-third of his estate, while the remainder goes to the Imam, since responsibility for his legal liability falls upon the Imam.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5694 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Aban and others, from Zurarah, from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"The Commander of the Faithful (as) ruled regarding the child of mula'anah that his mother inherits one-third, and the remainder belongs to the Imam because any liability for his actions falls upon the Imam."
